---
title: "Leadership"
---


Scientific leadership is about creating the conditions for excellent research that advances knowledge and helps address societal challenges. It involves fostering inclusive and collaborative environments where diverse perspectives, disciplines, and ways of knowing come together to generate innovative solutions for complex ocean sustainability issues. Effective leadership enables individuals and teams to thrive, supports creativity and innovation, builds research capacity, and strengthens the connections between science and society.

Throughout my career, I have sought to build interdisciplinary teams, develop international partnerships, mentor the next generation of researchers, and bridge science, policy, and practice. My approach is grounded in collaboration, integrity, inclusion, and shared purpose, with the goal of advancing scientific excellence while generating knowledge that informs decisions and contributes to a more sustainable and equitable future.

---

## Research Leadership

My research brings together marine ecology, climate science, fisheries, economics, and social sciences to understand how ocean systems respond to environmental change. I have led international collaborations involving universities, governments, NGOs, and intergovernmental organizations across multiple continents.

Current leadership roles include major international research projects, interdisciplinary synthesis activities, and collaborative networks focused on climate change, biodiversity, and sustainable oceans.

---

## Science for Policy

A central part of my work is ensuring that scientific knowledge informs decision-making.

I have contributed to major international assessments including the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and the Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services (IPBES). These assessments synthesize the best available scientific evidence to support governments in addressing climate change, biodiversity loss, food security, and sustainable development.

Beyond formal assessments, I work closely with governments, international organizations, and non-governmental organizations to co-develop evidence that supports practical policy and management decisions.

---

## Building Research Communities

Science advances through collaboration.

As former Director of the Institute for the Oceans and Fisheries at the University of British Columbia and founder of the Changing Ocean Research Unit (CORU), I have worked to create inclusive, interdisciplinary research environments where students, postdoctoral fellows, faculty, and partners can work together to tackle complex ocean challenges.

I believe that strong research communities are built on mutual respect, shared purpose, openness, and a commitment to scientific excellence.

---

## Mentorship

One of the most rewarding aspects of my career is mentoring students and early-career researchers.

I encourage independent thinking, interdisciplinary collaboration, and engagement beyond academia. Many former students and postdoctoral fellows now hold academic, government, and international leadership positions around the world.

Mentorship is not only about developing technical expertise—it is about helping researchers become thoughtful, collaborative, and impactful scientific leaders.

---

## Looking Forward

The challenges facing the ocean require science that is internationally connected, interdisciplinary, solution-oriented, and relevant to society.

I aim to contribute to a future in which scientific knowledge helps build resilient marine ecosystems, sustainable blue food systems, and equitable ocean governance for generations to come.
